thread:
jess_support: Heads-up — got a customer escalation: p95/p99 latency regressed after the canary rollout (v2.3.5) about 30m ago. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rt/latency?orgId=1
  p95 went from ~120ms to ~320ms, p99 from ~350ms to ~1.2s for the /v1/generate endpoint in us-west-2. Two paying customers hit timeouts and one reported intermittent 504s. Logs attached to the ticket. Anyone oncall?

mike_oncall: On it. Are we seeing QPS spikes or errors (OOMs, retries)? :eyes:

alex_runtime: I looked at node-level metrics — QPS steady, CPU normal, GPU util low on the canary hosts. Queue and kernel queueing latency spiked. Traces show long device syncs around first token generation for sequences >128. Link to trace waterfall: https://traces.redwood.example/trace/abcd1234

deploy-bot: Canary deploy v2.3.5 -> rollout started 2026-03-14T22:10Z (canary=15%).

sara_dev: Suggest we: 1) restrict canary to 5% immediately, 2) run a targeted replay against canary vs baseline, 3) prepare rollback if bisect points to runtime change. I can take traffic steering.

mike_oncall: Reduced canary to 5% (traffic-steer performed). Still seeing elevated p99 on the hosts that are on v2.3.5. Repro locally by curling host directly gives ~600–900ms tails when the host is running v2.3.5. Capturing flamegraph now.

alex_runtime: Copying useful commands for repro and quick toggle:
```bash
# replay a batch of requests against canary instances
replay-client --region us-west-2 --target canary --dataset ./repro/prompts_128.json --concurrency 8 --duration 5m
# toggle kernel selector override on a node (temporary)
sudo systemctl set-environment RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy && sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```
If the kernel selection is the culprit, forcing legacy should restore expected kernel path. I also see a recent commit that changed the heuristics for nvlink gather vs. host gather (commit abc123). It switches to the nvlink path for sequences >128 which on some firmware combos performs worse.

jess_support: Notifying affected customers with an ETA ~1h for mitigation. Any quick mitigations besides rollback? Could we pin to an older model variant or increase timeouts?

sara_dev: Quick mitigations in order: 1) steer production traffic for affected models back to v2.3.4 (done for two customers), 2) enable kernel selector env override on canary hosts as Alex suggested, 3) temporarily increase request timeout and enable more aggressive KV caching for prefix-heavy workloads. I've started traffic steering for the impacted tenants.

mike_oncall: I applied the env override on two canary hosts and p99 dropped from ~1.2s to ~230ms on those hosts within a couple minutes. Heap and dmesg show no OOMs. Looks kernel-selector related.

alex_runtime: Bisect notes: suspicious change = commit abc123 in runtime/exec/kernel_selector.cpp — adjusts nvlink threshold from 1024 -> 128. On older NVSwitch firmware this triggers an NVLink gather path with extra host syncs. Options: rollback commit (immediate) or ship hotfix to increase threshold back and add a firmware guard. Hotfix PR prepared: PR#4521.

sara_dev: Recommend hotfix to avoid broad rollback of unrelated changes. Plan: deploy PR#4521 to canary hosts, monitor p95/p99 for 15m, then roll to 30% and 100% if stable. Also add an alert that fires when p95 increases >2x AND canary fraction >0.

deploy-bot: Hotfix PR#4521 deployed to canary hosts at 2026-03-14T22:45Z (canary=5%).

mike_oncall: Monitoring — after hotfix p95 returned to ~140ms and p99 ~220ms on canary hosts. No new errors. Increasing canary to 30% now.

alex_runtime: Confirmed with replay load against hotfix canary: tails match baseline. Added a unit test for kernel selector heuristic to catch this on future firmware combos. Also adding a runway config to avoid nvlink path unless firmware >= X.Y.Z.

mike_oncall: Rolling to 100% now. Keeping an eye on saturations.

jess_support: Customers notified that we mitigated the issue and rolling fix is in. I'll close the escalations after final verification. Please add postmortem notes: root cause = kernel-selector heuristic change selecting nvlink gather for seq>128 which regressed performance on some infra firmware; mitigations = traffic steer, env override, hotfix PR that restores safe threshold + guard.

sara_dev: Filing a short postmortem and adding dashboard panels for kernel-selector version vs p95. Also adding an automated canary rollback policy when p99 > 2x baseline within 10m.

alex_runtime: One more follow-up: add a perf test to CI that replays a representative distribution of sequence lengths on multiple firmware images. That would have caught this. Will open a ticket.

jess_support: Thanks everyone. Great coordination. :tada:

mike_oncall: Nice work. I'll keep the incident channel open for 30m then archive.

sara_dev: Note: created ticket INF-7893 for the postmortem and remediation checklist.
